To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-based approach that reconstructs a 3D oral model using only ten 2D intraoral images captured from different angles, requiring no dedicated hardware devices. The proposed method reduces cost, eliminates the need for physical scanning equipment, minimises patient discomfort, and enables automated 3D reconstruction. The model is trained on the publicly available Dental3DS dataset, comprising 950 upper jaw samples, and employs MobileNetV2 as the image encoder combined with Multi-head Attention for multi-view feature fusion. The proposed model achieves an accuracy of 77.49%, measured by nearest-neighbor matching with a distance threshold of 0.035. However, predicted vertices tend to concentrate in high-density regions of the ground truth, resulting in uneven point distribution across the reconstructed model.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a cost-effective software-based approach for reconstructing 3D oral models using ten 2D images, overcoming limitations of conventional impression taking and intraoral scanning.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of traditional methods of oral modeling, including patient discomfort and high costs associated with intraoral scanners.
AI.method: The method reconstructs 3D models from ten 2D images using MobileNetV2 for image encoding and employs Multi-head Attention for feature fusion, trained on the Dental3DS dataset.
AI.result: The model achieved an accuracy of 77.49% in 3D reconstruction while facing challenges with uneven point distribution in high-density areas of the model.
AI.conclusion: The software-based approach presents an innovative solution that reduces costs and discomfort, though improvements are needed for point distribution in the resulting models.

title: CaliDist: Calibrating Large Language Models via Behavioral Robustness to Distraction
summary: Existing calibration methods for Large Language Models (LLMs) often overlook a critical dimension of trustworthiness: a model's {\em behavioral robustness} to irrelevant or misleading information. In this paper, we argue that a model's true confidence should reflect its stability under cognitive pressure. We introduce \textsc{CaliDist}, a novel post-hoc calibration approach that directly measures and penalizes a model's susceptibility to distraction. \textsc{CaliDist} quantifies how an LLM's predictions and uncertainty change when its input prompt is perturbed with semantic \textit{distractors}. This stability (or lack thereof) signal is then used to adaptively scale the model's initial confidence score. Our extensive experiments on seven Natural Language Understanding classification benchmarks using six distinct LLMs show that \textsc{CaliDist} consistently achieves lower Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Brier Score compared with strong baselines. Remarkably, our method reduces the ECE from 23\% to 7\% on average--a relative improvement of 70\%--demonstrating that behavioral stability is a powerful signal for calibration. We make our code and datasets available at github.com/m-anas-j/CaliDist.

AI.tldr: This paper presents 	extsc{CaliDist}, a post-hoc calibration technique for Large Language Models that improves model trustworthiness by measuring and addressing behavioral robustness under cognitive pressure from irrelevant information.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the inadequacy of existing calibration methods for LLMs by highlighting the importance of behavioral robustness to irrelevant or misleading information in assessing model trustworthiness.
AI.method: extsc{CaliDist} measures a model's susceptibility to semantic distractors by quantifying changes in predictions and uncertainty when the input prompt is perturbed. It adapts the model's initial confidence score based on this stability signal.
AI.result: The proposed 	extsc{CaliDist} method shows significant improvement over baseline methods, evidenced by a reduction in Expected Calibration Error (ECE) from 23% to 7% on average across seven benchmarks with six LLMs, representing a 70% relative improvement.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that behavioral stability is a crucial factor for achieving effective calibration in LLMs, with 	extsc{CaliDist} providing a promising solution to enhance model confidence assessment.

title: SALT: When More Rollouts Don't Help in Group-Based Policy Optimization and How to Make Them Matter
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) often adopts GRPO-style group-relative updates, sampling multiple rollouts per prompt to construct normalized learning signals. However, merely increasing the number of rollouts does not reliably strengthen learning: under GRPO-style group normalization, per-rollout policy-gradient features can concentrate into a low-rank, signed geometry, causing substantial cancellation during aggregation and weakening the effective update. We address this failure mode with SALT, a Subspace-Adaptive geometry pLug-in componenT that uses sample-wise gradient geometry to reweight the coefficients of group-relative updates. SALT estimates a dominant shared subspace from the mini-batch Gram geometry, decomposes group-relative coefficients into shared and residual channels, and adaptively amplifies the residual channel when signed cancellation is severe. Across diverse reasoning-oriented RLVR benchmarks and model scales, SALT improves effective update geometry and performance without modifying the reward model or the rollout sampling procedure

AI.tldr: The paper introduces SALT, a method to enhance reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by addressing issues in group-relative updates that cause ineffective learning due to low-rank geometry concentration.
AI.motivation: Traditional group-relative updates in RLVR do not effectively strengthen learning when simply increasing rollouts, leading to low effective updates due to cancellation effects.
AI.method: SALT uses sample-wise gradient geometry to reweight coefficients in group-relative updates by estimating a dominant subspace from mini-batch Gram geometry and amplifying the residual channel.
AI.result: SALT improves the effective update geometry and performance in various reasoning-oriented RLVR benchmarks and model scales without altering the reward model or sampling methods.
AI.conclusion: Implementing SALT effectively enhances learning dynamics in RLVR, mitigating cancellation effects in gradient updates.

title: Epistemic Injustice in Language Models: An Audit of Pretraining Filters and Guardrails
summary: Modern language models rely on pretraining filters to remove undesirable content from training corpora and inference-time guardrails to suppress undesirable outputs during deployment. In this paper, we examine how these filtering and moderation decisions produce forms of epistemic erasure and reveal tensions both across automated systems and between these systems and human judgment. We audit four pretraining filters and three inference-time guardrails on Common Crawl sentences containing gender and regional-origin mentions, together with a manually annotated subset of 500 sentences. Our analysis shows that filtering and guardrail decisions are strongly associated with blocklist-based lexical cues, while frequently failing to flag content containing private information or explicit hate speech. At the same time, marginalized groups, particularly transgender people, women, and Central Americans, are significantly over-flagged across systems. Human annotators, by contrast, would retain 88.5\% of filter-flagged and 91.3\% of guardrail-flagged content, often recognizing representational harms arising from tensions of content removal that current systems fail to capture. Taken together, our findings document a form of epistemic erasure in which mentions of marginalized groups are disproportionately removed before pretraining and additionally suppressed again at inference time.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how filtering and moderation systems in language models contribute to epistemic erasure, particularly affecting marginalized groups. It assesses the effectiveness of these systems and highlights discrepancies between automated and human judgment.
AI.motivation: To understand the impacts of filtering and moderation on the representation of marginalized groups in language models, specifically looking at epistemic erasure.
AI.method: An audit of four pretraining filters and three inference-time guardrails on datasets from Common Crawl, including a subset of 500 manually annotated sentences, assessing their impact on content mentioning gender and regional origins.
AI.result: Filtering and guardrail decisions mainly rely on blocklist cues, often missing elements like private information or hate speech, while over-flagging content related to marginalized communities. Human annotators would retain a large majority of flagged content, recognizing issues of representational harm that automated systems overlook.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals that automated filtering processes contribute to epistemic erasure by disproportionately removing mentions of marginalized groups, indicating a need for improved systems that align better with human judgment.

title: ATT-CR: Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal
summary: Cloud removal aims to accurately reconstruct the ground objects obscured by clouds in remote sensing images. Existing Transformer-based methods utilizing self-attention have shown impressive results by effectively modeling long-range dependencies in cloudy images. However, they suffer from the following issues: 1) the high computational complexity of self-attention limits scalability; 2) treating both cloudy and clean pixels as valid within the attention computation brings disturbances in subsequent layers, leading to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose the Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal (ATT-CR), a model that effectively reduces computational costs and mitigates interference from cloudy pixels. Specifically, it consists of two core components: Triangular Attention (TAN) and Feature Selected Gating Module (FSGM). TAN employs lower and upper triangular matrices to approximate Softmax attention with O(N) computational complexity, significantly reducing the computational costs. The FSGM, on the other hand, integrates with TAN to adaptively distinguish between cloudy and clean features, which minimizes the introduction of invalid information into subsequent layers. Extensive experiments on cloud removal benchmarks demonstrate that ATT-CR delivers superior performance compared to existing methods.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Adaptive Triangular Transformer for Cloud Removal (ATT-CR), addressing the limitations of existing Transformer-based methods in remote sensing image cloud removal by reducing computational complexity and filtering out invalid pixel information.
AI.motivation: There is a need for effective cloud removal methods in remote sensing images that overcome the high computational complexity and performance degradation caused by including cloudy pixels in self-attention computations.
AI.method: The ATT-CR model incorporates two key components: Triangular Attention (TAN) for reduced computational complexity and Feature Selected Gating Module (FSGM) to distinguish between cloudy and clean features.
AI.result: Experiments show that ATT-CR significantly outperforms existing cloud removal methods on benchmark datasets.
AI.conclusion: ATT-CR offers an efficient and effective solution for cloud removal in remote sensing images, improving performance while addressing existing method limitations.

title: Robust and sparse support vector machine via hybrid truncated loss for supervised classification
summary: The support vector machine (SVM) is a widely used classifier, but choosing an appropriate loss function remains difficult. Convex losses such as the hinge loss and least-squares loss are sensitive to outliers, while bounded non-convex losses often lead to high computational cost. To address this, we propose a hybrid truncated loss function ($L_{\mathrm{ht}}$) that is both sparse and bounded, and build the $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM model for single-view classification. We introduce the P-stationary point and use it to establish the first-order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions. Based on these conditions, we design an alternating direction method of multipliers with a working-set strategy that reduces computational cost and achieves global convergence. We further extend $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM to multi-view learning by adding structural information and view weights, resulting in Mv$L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM, which follows both the consensus and complementarity principles. Experiments on synthetic, real-world, and image datasets show that $L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM achieves higher accuracy with fewer support vectors and better noise robustness than five single-view methods, while Mv$L_{\mathrm{ht}}$-SVM outperforms six multi-view methods in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a hybrid truncated loss function for support vector machines to improve classification performance, particularly with outliers and computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this research is to enhance the performance of support vector machines by finding a loss function that balances sensitivity to outliers and computational complexity.
AI.method: The authors propose a hybrid truncated loss function ($L_{ht}$) and establish an alternating direction method of multipliers for optimization, ensuring global convergence and reducing computational costs.
AI.result: The proposed $L_{ht}$-SVM shows superior accuracy, fewer support vectors, and better robustness to noise compared to existing single-view classifiers, while the Mv$L_{ht}$-SVM excels in multi-view settings across various performance metrics.
AI.conclusion: The research concludes that the hybrid truncated loss function significantly improves both single-view and multi-view classification tasks, proving its effectiveness in practical applications.

title: Global-Local Monte Carlo Tree Search in Vision-Language Models for Text-to-3D Indoor Scene Generation
summary: Large Vision-Language Models have achieved significant reasoning performance in various tasks.However, there are few studies on text-to-3D indoor scene generation with LVLMs. The main challenge is that prevailing LVLM-based methods employ chain-of-thought sequential decision mechanisms that cannot revise earlier decisions, causing error propagation.In this paper, we consider the task as a planning problem constrained by spatial and layout commonsense.To solve this problem, we model it as a tree search problem with global and local trees, which differs from existing sequential decision-making approaches.In the global tree, we place each object iteratively and explore multiple attempts like humans furnishing a room, where the problem space is represented as a tree.To effectively search the tree, we propose a hierarchical scene representation and a PRM-guided MCTS method.The hierarchical representation abstracts a scene into room level, region level, floor object level, and supported object level.The PRM-guided MCTS method uses the PRM to prune unnecessary branches and the MCTS algorithm to balance exploration and exploitation to get an optimal solution with fewer attempts.In the local tree, it further decomposes the placement of each object into finer sub-steps, including the specific placement parameters.To make the whole appearance of the scene consistent, we leverage pre-trained diffusion image generative models to predict textures for all the objects in the scene.As existing benchmarks for text-to-3D indoor scene generation remain limited in scale and diversity, we collect a new large-scale diverse dataset that contains 65 scene types and 3,250 instructions with diverse sizes, layouts, and styles, named 3DTindo-bench, to better assess the capability of the state-of-the-art models. Our experiments show that our method generates more realistic 3D scenes than state-of-the-art approaches.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses text-to-3D indoor scene generation using Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), proposing a novel planning approach based on tree search to avoid errors in sequential decision-making. It introduces a hierarchical scene representation and a PRM-guided MCTS method for improved object placement.
AI.motivation: To enhance text-to-3D indoor scene generation, as existing LVLM methods struggle with error propagation due to their chained sequential decision-making.
AI.method: The study models the scene generation as a planning problem through a tree search framework, utilizing hierarchical scene representation and a PRM-guided MCTS method for optimized object placement.
AI.result: The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in generating more realistic 3D scenes, supported by a new dataset (3DTindo-bench) with 65 scene types and 3,250 diverse instructions.
AI.conclusion: The new approach effectively generates realistic indoor scenes while addressing limitations of current benchmarks and methodologies.

title: Large Language Models are Perplexed by some Political Parties
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used, including in political applications, but their political fairness has been little studied. We assess it using perplexity, posing that a fair model should give equal probability to all political groups. However, we find, across ten LLMs and three datasets covering 37 languages, that LLMs are more perplexed by the texts of far right and nationalist parties than of social-democratic parties. We find this to be consistent with previous work on translation fairness, to the point that perplexity correlates with downstream translation metrics. Our method is applicable to both base LLMs as well as their instruction-tuned counterpart, and we find that both are highly correlated, suggesting that the political fairness of LLMs stems from their pretraining, and is hardly affected by instruction-tuning.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the political fairness of Large Language Models (LLMs) by assessing perplexity across various political texts and languages, revealing bias against far right and nationalist parties.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the political fairness of LLMs, which are being increasingly utilized in political contexts, yet have not been adequately assessed for bias among various political groups.
AI.method: The study measures perplexity of texts from different political parties across ten LLMs and three datasets in 37 languages to determine the models' response to various political ideologies.
AI.result: LLMs exhibited higher perplexity when processing texts from far right and nationalist parties compared to social-democratic parties, indicating bias; this aligns with previous findings on translation fairness, showing a correlation between perplexity and translation metrics.
AI.conclusion: The political fairness observed in LLMs appears rooted in their pretraining data, with minimal effect from instruction-tuning, suggesting inherent biases based on the types of texts encountered during training.

title: Consistency Training Along the Transformer Stack
summary: Consistency training encourages models to behave similarly across different contexts, and has shown promise for reducing misalignment. We broaden the scope of consistency training in two ways. First, we introduce two new internal consistency targets: MLP Consistency Training (MLPCT), which matches post-activation MLP states, and Attention Consistency Training (AttCT), which matches per-head attention distributions. Second, we apply consistency training to four additional safety threats: persona in-context learning attacks, adversarial frustration, prefill attacks, and conditional misalignment. Across several models and threat settings, we find that consistency training reduces misalignment well beyond the sycophancy and jailbreak settings studied in prior work. We also find cases of cross-threat generalization, where training against one failure mode improves robustness to another, and identify a shared residual-stream mechanism underlying ACT, MLPCT, and AttCT, while distinguishing BCT as mechanistically distinct. Our results suggest that consistency training is a flexible and extensible framework for alignment, capable of unifying defenses against a broader class of model pathologies.

AI.tldr: This paper expands consistency training by introducing new internal consistency targets and applying it to additional safety threats, leading to improved model alignment and robustness across various failure modes.
AI.motivation: To enhance model alignment and robustness against a wider range of safety threats.
AI.method: Introduces MLP Consistency Training (MLPCT) and Attention Consistency Training (AttCT) as new internal targets, and applies consistency training to various safety threats.
AI.result: Demonstrated that consistency training significantly reduces misalignment in models beyond previously studied settings and reveals cross-threat generalization benefits.
AI.conclusion: Consistency training proves to be a versatile and effective framework for model alignment and defense against diverse pathologies.

title: Measuring the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction to prompt, model, and schema choices in clinical discharge summaries
comment: 69 pages, 5 main figures, supplementary material included
summary: Large language models are increasingly used for structured extraction from clinical free-text notes, but the sensitivity of their output to upstream configuration choices is less understood than their accuracy on fixed benchmarks. This work measures that sensitivity without human-annotated ground truth, by holding the extraction task fixed and varying one choice at a time. The fixed schema comprises 17 clinical documentation flags on a three-way yes/no/not_documented value set and a 47-tag vocabulary for the primary admission reason. Three prompt variants expressing this schema were each run at two model sizes on MIMIC-IV v3.1 discharge summaries. Cross-prompt agreement was measured by Cohen's kappa on ICD-stratified subsets. A paired same-note comparison isolated the effect of model choice, and a post-hoc collapse of the three-way flags to binary tested the schema's contribution to disagreement. On the three-way flags, the two models reach the same pooled cross-prompt agreement (median kappa 0.69 and 0.68); the larger model raises agreement on some fields and lowers it on others, a redistribution rather than the absence of an effect. Collapsing the schema to binary dissolves most of the cross-prompt disagreement, locating it on the absence-versus-silence distinction rather than on whether the finding is present. On the multi-class admission categorization, changing the model reassigns the dominant tag on close to half of all notes while changing the prompt phrasing reassigns it on roughly one in eight, and the larger model places far less mass on residual catch-all categories (44% to 26%). These patterns indicate a schema-imposed source of disagreement concentrated on the absence-versus-silence axis and a dominance of model over prompt phrasing on multi-class categorization, identified by a reusable methodology for auditing extraction reproducibility on a population-scale deployment.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes the sensitivity of large language models in structured extraction from clinical notes by varying upstream configuration choices, revealing significant effects of model size and schema on extraction outcomes.
AI.motivation: To understand how configuration choices impact the output sensitivity of large language models in clinical text extraction, beyond mere accuracy on benchmarks.
AI.method: The study involved running three prompt variants at two model sizes on MIMIC-IV v3.1 discharge summaries, measuring cross-prompt agreement using Cohen's kappa and examining differences through a paired same-note comparison.
AI.result: The larger model affects agreement variably across fields, with schema changes mainly impacting absence versus silence distinctions; model changes significantly influence multi-class admission categorization, altering dominant tags in many cases.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes that there is a schema-related source of disagreement in clinical extraction, with model choice exerting a greater influence than prompt phrasing, providing a method for assessing extraction reproducibility in large-scale applications.

title: ReSAGE-PAR: Representational Similarity Assessment for Generative Expansion in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
comment: Under review at IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (TCSVT)
summary: To address the limited diversity and data scarcity in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR), we explore image synthesis using diffusion models guided by attribute-based prompts. While this enables the controlled generation of pedestrian images, it faces two critical challenges: (i) the domain gap between high-quality pre-training data and low-resolution, non-standard surveillance crops, and (ii) the need for reliable attribute verification to prevent generative hallucinations. In this paper, we introduce a robust generate-score-autolabel pipeline called ReSAGE-PAR (REpresentational Similarity Assessment for Generative Expansion in PAR) that bridges this domain gap and enables scalable, high-fidelity dataset expansion. First, we adapt pre-trained diffusion models to native PAR resolutions using a tailored LoRA-based Image-to-Image approach. Second, we extract vision-language alignment scores between the generated images and their conditioning prompts, utilizing a comprehensive prompting strategy that includes label-consistent and inconsistent complements. Finally, we formulate a Bayesian classifier that converts these continuous scores into reliable binary pseudo-labels. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of ReSAGE-PAR in preserving spatial priors and verifying attributes. When integrated into PAR training, ReSAGE-PAR consistently yields significant improvements-achieving gains of up to 8.7% on standard backbones and pushing state-of-the-art frameworks to new performance levels. This proves its value as an architecture-agnostic solution for scalable PAR enhancement. The complete codebase for ReSAGE-PAR is publicly available at http://www-vpu.eps.uam.es/publications/ReSAGE-PAR.

AI.tldr: This paper presents ReSAGE-PAR, a pipeline that addresses data scarcity in Pedestrian Attribute Recognition (PAR) by generating high-quality images using diffusion models, overcoming domain gaps and ensuring attribute reliability, resulting in significant performance improvements in PAR tasks.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses challenges in PAR related to limited data diversity and the quality of images obtained from surveillance systems.
AI.method: ReSAGE-PAR utilizes diffusion models to generate pedestrian images, adapts pre-trained models to specific resolutions, assesses vision-language alignment scores, and employs a Bayesian classifier for creating binary pseudo-labels.
AI.result: The extensive evaluations demonstrate that ReSAGE-PAR enhances performance significantly, achieving up to 8.7% improvements on standard neural network architectures.
AI.conclusion: ReSAGE-PAR serves as an architecture-agnostic solution that enhances the scalability and fidelity of datasets used in PAR.

title: Beyond Alignment: Value Diversity as a Collective Property in Multicultural Agent Systems
summary: Multicultural multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed in globally diverse settings, where different agents are grounded in different cultural backgrounds. Existing cultural evaluation focuses on value alignment: how closely a single agent matches a target culture. Yet alignment is a per-agent property and cannot reveal whether a system, taken as a whole, preserves the cultural plurality it is meant to represent. We propose value diversity as a system-level evaluation axis for multicultural agent systems, defined through the dissimilarity between culturally conditioned agents' responses on a shared value survey. Using the World Values Survey, we evaluate 19 cultures and 18 backbone models across a wide range of system configurations. We find that diversity is largely uncorrelated with alignment, indicating that the two capture complementary system properties, and that current multicultural agent systems fall substantially below human societies in value diversity. Mixed-backbone systems narrow this gap but do not close it, and the gap persists across culture compositions and agent scales. Social interaction further erodes diversity by driving agents toward consensus, and a participatory budgeting case study shows that this homogenization narrows the breadth of collective decision-making. Together, our results establish value diversity as a distinct evaluation axis for multicultural multi-agent systems and reveal a persistent homogenization tendency in current LLM-based societies. Our code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/iNLP-Lab/MultiAgent-Diversity.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces value diversity as a novel evaluation axis for multicultural multi-agent systems, highlighting the disparity in value representation compared to human societies and the tendency towards homogenization in agent interactions.
AI.motivation: The need for a comprehensive evaluation of multicultural multi-agent systems that goes beyond individual value alignment to assess the preservation of cultural diversity within the system as a whole.
AI.method: The study employs the World Values Survey to analyze responses from 19 cultures and 18 backbone models, measuring dissimilarity in agent responses across various configurations.
AI.result: Findings indicate a lack of correlation between value diversity and alignment, with current systems demonstrating lower diversity compared to human societies; mixed-backbone approaches improve but do not eliminate this gap.
AI.conclusion: The research establishes value diversity as an essential evaluation criterion for multicultural multi-agent systems and underscores a significant trend towards homogenization, particularly in decision-making processes.

title: GenAutoML: An Agentic Framework for Dynamic Architecture Generation and Optimization in Time-Series Analysis
summary: Designing neural architectures for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection remains a resource-intensive task that often requires substantial domain expertise. Traditional Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) systems typically rely on static, predefined search spaces, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse data characteristics. We present GenAutoML, an agentic framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) as neural architects to bridge natural-language requirements and executable PyTorch implementations. The framework incorporates a Sandboxed Reflection Loop for autonomous code refinement and a Signature-Aware Runtime that enforces architectural consistency and execution safety. To improve robustness under non-stationary conditions, we further introduce a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization (Dyn-RevIN) wrapper. Experiments on the ETTh1, ETTm1, and Weather benchmarks demonstrate that GenAutoML can dynamically generate task-specific neural architectures tailored to dataset characteristics. Among the generated models, WaveInterferenceNet achieves inference latency below 0.01 ms per sample while maintaining competitive predictive performance. By emphasizing computational efficiency, architectural adaptability, and stable optimization behavior, GenAutoML enables the creation of ultra-lightweight neural networks suitable for resource-constrained and latency-sensitive Edge AI deployments.

AI.tldr: GenAutoML is an innovative framework that uses Large Language Models for automating the design of neural architectures for time-series forecasting and anomaly detection, incorporating dynamic features for improved robustness and efficiency.
AI.motivation: To alleviate the resource-intensive nature of designing neural architectures for time-series tasks, especially in the context of varying data characteristics and without necessitating extensive domain expertise.
AI.method: GenAutoML uses Large Language Models to translate natural-language requirements into PyTorch neural network implementations, includes a Sandboxed Reflection Loop for code refinement, and employs a Dynamic Reversible Instance Normalization wrap for robustness under changing conditions.
AI.result: GenAutoML dynamically creates task-specific neural architectures for different benchmarks, with WaveInterferenceNet achieving remarkable inference efficiency and competitive prediction accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The framework supports the development of ultra-lightweight neural networks, making it suitable for constrained environments like Edge AI, through enhanced computational efficiency, architectural adaptability, and stable optimization.

title: Texture-preserving implicit neural representation for Cone beam CT truncated reconstruction
summary: Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) frequently suffers from data truncation, which introduces severe artifacts and limits the effective field of view (FOV). Existing deep learning methods for truncated cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) reconstruction suffer from serious limitations, including a strict reliance on supervised ground truth and a failure to account for continuous 3D spatial truncation variations. To address these challenges, we introduce a self-supervised 3D reconstruction framework based on neural scene representations. By directly mapping spatial coordinates to radiodensity under projection supervision, our approach inherently bypasses traditional filtering and backprojection operations, thereby fundamentally eliminating truncation-induced ring artifacts while enabling robust continuous 3D data extrapolation. However, coordinate networks are susceptible to an inherent spectral bias, which leads to a severe loss of clinically vital high-frequency textures. To resolve this bottleneck, we further incorporate a physics-based iterative refinement module into the neural scene representation architecture. Leveraging the artifact-free, extrapolated volume from the coordinate network as an optimal initialization, this module progressively re-extracts and injects high-frequency structural information from the original projections back into the volume. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that our method successfully unifies the exceptional artifact suppression and extrapolation capabilities of neural networks with the high-fidelity detail preservation of iterative algorithms.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a self-supervised 3D reconstruction framework for truncated cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) that combines neural scene representations with a physics-based iterative refinement module, improving artifact suppression and high-frequency detail preservation.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this work is to overcome limitations in existing CBCT reconstruction methods, specifically their reliance on supervised learning and inability to handle variations in spatial truncation.
AI.method: A self-supervised framework is developed using neural scene representations, mapping spatial coordinates to radiodensity under projection supervision, and enhanced with a physics-based iterative refinement module to recover high-frequency textures.
AI.result: The proposed method effectively eliminates truncation-induced artifacts and enables robust continuous 3D data extrapolation while preserving high-frequency details through iterative refinement.
AI.conclusion: Experimental results on simulated and real-world data show that the method successfully integrates neural networks' artifact suppression with the fidelity of traditional iterative techniques.

title: The Generator-Eraser Paradox: Community Guidelines for Responsible LLM-Assisted Dialect Resource Creation
summary: Dialect resources occupy a unique position at the intersection of scientific description, cultural preservation, and computational infrastructure. Large language models offer powerful capabilities for accelerating dialect resource development through retrieval-grounded drafting, corpus navigation, metadata enrichment, and annotation workflow support. However, the same systems pose substantial risks: they can contribute to dialect erasure by privileging prestige varieties, homogenizing orthography, and enabling synthetic feedback loops that reduce linguistic diversity over time. These risks are particularly acute for language varieties characterized by diglossia, limited written standardization, or marginalized speaker communities. This paper makes three contributions. First, we integrate insights from variationist sociolinguistics and corpus linguistics to formalize the generator-eraser paradox as a theoretical framework for understanding the dual nature of LLM-assisted dialect work. Second, we derive 12 community guidelines that operationalize this framework into implementable design requirements for dialect resource creation and documentation. Third, we provide an in-depth case study of Arabic dialects, including a structured comparison of widely used resources, to demonstrate how these guidelines address language-specific challenges including diglossia, orthographic variability, and community governance. The contribution is conceptual and operational rather than experimental, with the goal of enabling dialect communities and resource builders across languages to adopt LLMs without sacrificing authenticity, variation, or sovereignty.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the benefits and risks of using large language models (LLMs) in the development of dialect resources, proposing a framework and guidelines to ensure linguistic diversity is maintained.
AI.motivation: The study aims to address the potential benefits of LLMs in dialect resource creation while acknowledging the risks they pose for dialect erasure, particularly for marginalized communities.
AI.method: The authors synthesize insights from sociolinguistics and corpus linguistics to develop the generator-eraser paradox as a framework and create 12 community guidelines for dialect resource development.
AI.result: A detailed case study on Arabic dialects illustrates how the proposed guidelines can mitigate risks associated with LLMs and address specific language challenges such as diglossia and orthographic variability.
AI.conclusion: The paper emphasizes the importance of adopting LLMs in dialect work thoughtfully to preserve authenticity, variation, and community sovereignty.

title: LoomVideo: Unifying Multimodal Inputs into Video Generation and Editing
summary: Developing unified video generation and editing models capable of interpreting interleaved multimodal inputs is a promising yet challenging frontier field. Existing unified frameworks predominantly rely on massive models (typically 13B parameters or more) and incorporate source video conditions for editing by concatenating sequence tokens. This concatenation inevitably doubles the sequence length, quadrupling the computational complexity of the self-attention mechanism and introducing prohibitive overhead. To address these bottlenecks, we present LoomVideo, a highly efficient 5B-parameter unified architecture for both video generation and editing. LoomVideo replaces the standard text encoder with a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) and employs Deepstack injection mechanism to align multi-layer MLLM features with the Diffusion Transformer (DiT). Crucially, we introduce a zero-overhead Scale-and-Add conditioning approach for video editing. By scaling and directly adding the clean source video latent to the noised target latent, this elegant design eliminates the need for token concatenation, drastically reducing computational cost while maintaining robust capabilities for complex, non-rigid edits. Furthermore, a Negative Temporal RoPE strategy is seamlessly integrated to handle multiple reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our compact 5B model achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across comprehensive benchmarks, exhibiting exceptional superiority in e-commerce and fashion generation scenarios. Benefiting from the zero-overhead conditioning mechanism, LoomVideo achieves at least a 5.41x acceleration in inference speed compared to models of similar capabilities, paving the way for highly practical and efficient video foundation models.

AI.tldr: LoomVideo is a 5B-parameter model for video generation and editing that overcomes the inefficiencies of larger models by using a novel zero-overhead conditioning mechanism, achieving state-of-the-art performance with significant speed improvements.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient unified architecture for video generation and editing that handles multimodal inputs without the computational burden of larger models.
AI.method: LoomVideo employs a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) and a Deepstack injection mechanism, introducing a zero-overhead Scale-and-Add conditioning approach to eliminate token concatenation in video editing.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show that LoomVideo achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on comprehensive benchmarks, particularly in e-commerce and fashion generation, while attaining at least a 5.41x acceleration in inference speed.
AI.conclusion: LoomVideo provides a practical and efficient solution for video foundation models, demonstrating significant advancements in performance and computational efficiency.

title: TS-ICL: A Flexible Time-Indexed Foundation Model for Time Series via In-Context Learning
summary: Foundation models mark a profound paradigm shift in time series modeling, with task-specific models being superseded by general-purpose zero-shot models. Yet, current approaches primarily focus on forecasting, while real-world time series are often irregularly and partially observed, requiring models that can jointly forecast, impute missing values, and handle degraded sampling conditions. To address these challenges, we introduce TS-ICL, a novel probabilistic In-Context Learning encoder--regressor Transformer that unifies forecasting and imputation. TS-ICL formulates time series tasks as timestamp-aligned regression and naturally incorporates covariates by training on synthetic dependency structures generated from a novel causal data prior. Empirically, TS-ICL achieves a new state-of-the-art in imputation, while remaining competitive with leading forecasting foundation models across both univariate and covariate-aware benchmarks. It shows particularly strong performance in forecasting with partially observed look-back windows.

AI.tldr: TS-ICL is a novel probabilistic In-Context Learning model that unifies forecasting and imputation of time series data, outperforming existing models in imputation while remaining competitive in forecasting tasks.
AI.motivation: To address the limitations of existing time series models that primarily focus on forecasting, and to effectively manage irregular and partially observed data.
AI.method: A probabilistic encoder--regressor Transformer called TS-ICL is proposed, which formulates tasks as timestamp-aligned regression and integrates covariates using synthetic dependency structures from a causal data prior.
AI.result: TS-ICL achieves new state-of-the-art results in imputation and demonstrates competitive performance in forecasting across various benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: TS-ICL effectively combines forecasting and imputation, particularly excelling in scenarios with partially observed data.

title: Deciphering Two Training Clocks in Grokking via Deep Linear Network Theory with Conditional ReLU Reduction
summary: Grokking suggests that fitting the training data and learning a simple underlying rule may occur on different time scales. We formalize this phenomenon by separating the fast decay of the classification loss from the slower simplification of the learned representation, and we call the resulting pair of stopping times two training clocks. For deep linear networks, we show that a post-margin gap-growth or one-step tail-contraction condition reduces the cross-entropy loss to level epsilon on a logarithmic time scale. In contrast, when layerwise weight decay is present, the induced regularization on the end-to-end map can be expressed as a Schatten-type penalty; under a sharp late-time Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz tail, this structural energy closes on a polynomial time scale. The two clocks, therefore, separate fitting from representation simplification. We then explain how the same mechanism can appear in ReLU MLPs. In regions where the activation patterns on the training set remain fixed, the network reduces to a linear model in the active coordinates. In a two-layer ReLU embedding model, chain-rule estimates further show that the classifier head can receive larger effective gradients than the embedding block under controlled downstream norms. This supports a two-stage mechanism in which the classifier fits first, while the representation continues to simplify later. We use modular addition as the main experimental setting. The deep linear theory provides the rigorous core of the analysis. But the ReLU results are formulated as conditional reductions that account for empirical behavior without claiming a global proof for nonlinear training dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the phenomenon of 'grokking' in deep learning, where fitting training data and simplifying learned representations occur on different time scales, introducing the concept of two training clocks. It presents a formal analysis for deep linear networks and explores the mechanisms in ReLU MLPs without offering definitive global proofs for nonlinear dynamics.
AI.motivation: The study of grokking aims to understand why fitting a model to training data and learning a simple underlying rule happens at different rates, with implications for training dynamics in neural networks.
AI.method: The paper formalizes grokking by defining two training clocks that separate the rapid decay of classification loss from slower representation simplification. It employs mathematical analysis on deep linear networks and offers insights into ReLU MLPs through the lens of modular addition as a simple experimental setting.
AI.result: For deep linear networks, a condition for margin growth allows the reduction of the cross-entropy loss to a logarithmic time scale, while weight decay results in a polynomial time scale of convergence, demonstrating the separation of fitting and representation simplification. It presents evidence from ReLU networks showing that as certain activation patterns stabilize, training dynamics reflect a two-stage mechanism.
AI.conclusion: The research articulates distinct training dynamics in neural networks, highlighting a foundational rigorous analysis for deep linear models while suggesting additional conditional insights for ReLU MLPs. This underscores a two-stage training process where classifier fitting occurs before continued simplification of the representation.

title: LLM-Conditioned Synthesis of Pathological Gaits via Structured Gait-Language Representations
comment: Accepted at CVPR MOMA Workshop 2026 and selected for spotlight presentation at the workshop
summary: Pathological gait datasets remain scarce due to privacy, recruitment, cost, and movement variability. Our work presents a multimodal LLM-guided framework for pathology-aware 3D gait data synthesis from structured textual descriptions. The proposed method generates fixed-length synthetic skeleton-based gait sequences for pathological gait classification tasks. The framework combines motion tokenisation, pathology-aware language conditioning, LLM-based semantic augmentation, and language-to-gait generation. A key contribution is the proposed pathological tokeniser, which is designed to preserve pathology-specific motion characteristics during discrete representation learning. Experiments suggest that the proposed synthetic sequences improve downstream classification for recurrent classifiers when combined with real data. The best result is obtained using a GRU classifier trained with real and synthetic samples, achieving 92.77\% accuracy under a leave-one-subject-out protocol.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a framework for generating synthetic 3D gait data from textual descriptions to aid in pathological gait classification, using a novel tokeniser that preserves motion characteristics.
AI.motivation: To address the scarcity of pathological gait datasets caused by privacy, recruitment, and variability issues, which hampers research and development in this area.
AI.method: The framework employs motion tokenisation, combines it with pathology-aware language conditioning, LLM for semantic augmentation, and translates language into gait data generation, focusing on a pathological tokeniser to maintain motion characteristics.
AI.result: Synthetic gait sequences significantly enhance the classification accuracy of recurrent classifiers when used alongside real data, with a GRU classifier achieving 92.77% accuracy in a leave-one-subject-out validation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method effectively generates useful synthetic data for improving pathological gait classification, demonstrating the potential of combining language models with gait analysis.

title: When Denser Credit Is Not Enough: Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Training
summary: Long-horizon LLM agents require reinforcement learning methods that can assign credit to intermediate decisions under sparse and delayed rewards. Recent group-based methods such as GiGPO improve over GRPO by constructing step-level advantages at repeated anchor states. However, we show that such dense credit can be statistically unreliable: under limited rollouts, rare but lucky actions may receive overly large advantages, producing divergent anchor bias and late-stage training oscillation. We propose Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization (ECPO), a critic-free policy optimization algorithm that calibrates step-level credit before policy updates. ECPO combines Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which groups rollouts by canonical actions and shrinks low-count estimates, with Variance-Gated Credit Weighting, which suppresses anchor states dominated by within-action noise. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B show that ECPO consistently outperforms strong baselines, improving GiGPO by +5.2/+7.3 success points on ALFWorld/WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B while adding only 0.1% additional advantage-computation overhead.

AI.tldr: Evidence-Calibrated Policy Optimization (ECPO) enhances reinforcement learning for LLM agents by addressing credit assignment issues in group-based methods, particularly improving stability and performance in sparse reward environments.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of credit assignment in long-horizon reinforcement learning where rewards are sparse and delayed, particularly the statistical unreliability in group-based methods like GiGPO.
AI.method: ECPO is a critic-free policy optimization algorithm that combines Evidence-Calibrated Action Advantage, which improves the accuracy of estimates for actions with low samples, and Variance-Gated Credit Weighting to reduce the influence of high-variance anchor states.
AI.result: ECPO consistently outperforms strong baseline methods, achieving +5.2 success points on ALFWorld and +7.3 on WebShop with minimal overhead in advantage computation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed ECPO method leads to improved stability and performance in reinforcement learning tasks, showcasing its effectiveness over existing methods.

title: Contextualized Prompting For Stance Detection On Social Media
summary: Stance detection on social media is challenging due to short, noisy, and context-dependent language. While large language models (LLMs) show zero-shot generalization, they are typically prompted without contextual information, which limits their ability to interpret ambiguous posts. In this work, we systematically investigate the impact of incorporating real-world (e.g., user biographies), derived (e.g., political party), and LLM-generated (e.g., target descriptions) contextual features into zero-shot prompting for stance detection on Twitter. Our evaluation spans four benchmark datasets, including a new high-quality German Twitter stance dataset. Across multiple LLMs, we find that integrating contextual information improves performance, but only under specific conditions. LLM-generated target descriptions consistently enhance accuracy, while other user metadata has mixed or even detrimental effects. Notably, we show that the inclusion of other tweets by the same user, often beneficial in supervised learning, can impair performance due to input noise. Our qualitative analysis reveals that LLMs struggle to distinguish task-specific useful information from irrelevant context. Our findings highlight both the promise and challenges of prompting with context information in noisy real-world settings. We publish code and data at this \href{https://github.com/tilmanbeck/stance-context-twitter}{page}.

AI.tldr: This paper studies stance detection on Twitter using contextual features with large language models (LLMs), showing both improvements and challenges in performance based on the type of context used.
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy of stance detection on social media by utilizing contextual information that can aid language models in interpreting ambiguous posts.
AI.method: The research evaluates the effect of various contextual features (real-world, derived, and LLM-generated) on four benchmark datasets, including a new German Twitter dataset, through zero-shot prompting for stance detection.
AI.result: Integrating contextual information generally improves performance; LLM-generated target descriptions enhance accuracy, while other user metadata can be mixed or detrimental. Importantly, user tweets’ inclusion can impair performance due to noise.
AI.conclusion: The study emphasizes the potential benefits and limitations of using contextual features in stance detection, revealing that LLMs have difficulty in filtering relevant information from noisy context.

title: EGTR-Review: Efficient Evidence-Grounded Scientific Peer Review Generation via Multi-Agent Teacher Distillation
summary: Scientific peer review generation has attracted increasing attention for reducing reviewing burdens and providing timely feedback. However, existing Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods often produce generic comments with insufficient evidence support and weak source traceability, while complex multi-agent systems incur high inference costs. To address these challenges, we propose EGTR-Review, an Evidence-Grounded and Traceable Review Generation framework via Multi-Agent Teacher Distillation. EGTR-Review first constructs a multi-agent teacher that performs structure-aware paper decomposition, key-element extraction, external scholarly evidence retrieval, evidence-state labeling, verification reasoning, and review synthesis. It then distills both intermediate reasoning trajectories and final review comments into a lightweight student model through task-prefix-driven multi-task learning. An evidence-weighted objective further reduces the influence of weak, missing, or non-verifiable supervision. Experiments on public peer-review datasets show that EGTR-Review (Student) outperforms strong prompt-based, fine-tuned, and structured/agentic baselines across automatic metrics, LLM-as-Judge evaluation, and human evaluation, while maintaining strong factual grounding and source traceability with substantially lower token consumption and inference time. Our code, prompts, configurations, and sample data are available on GitHub.

AI.tldr: EGTR-Review is a framework for generating scientific peer reviews, overcoming limitations of existing LLM methods by providing evidence-based, traceable, and cost-effective solutions through a multi-agent approach and distillation.
AI.motivation: To reduce reviewing burdens and enhance the quality of peer reviews by addressing the limitations of current LLM-based methods, such as generic comments and high inference costs.
AI.method: EGTR-Review utilizes a multi-agent teacher model for paper decomposition, key-element extraction, evidence retrieval, and synthesis, followed by a lightweight student model to distill knowledge using multi-task learning and evidence-weighted objectives.
AI.result: EGTR-Review achieves superior performance across various evaluation metrics compared to existing methods while ensuring strong factual grounding and traceability.
AI.conclusion: The framework significantly reduces token consumption and inference time while improving the quality of peer reviews, making it a valuable tool for the scientific community.

title: High-Dimensional Theory of LoRA Fine-Tuning in a Solvable Attention Model
summary: We develop a high-dimensional statistical theory of low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in attention models, capturing the interplay between pre-training and fine-tuning. We introduce a solvable framework in which a single-head attention layer is first pre-trained on a data-abundant task and subsequently adapted via a rank-one LoRA update on limited data. In the high-dimensional limit, both stages admit a sharp asymptotic characterization in terms of a finite set of order parameters, yielding explicit predictions for test errors and representation alignment. Our analysis shows that the impact of pre-training on LoRA is summarized by an effective noise term, from which we derive prescriptions for the optimal pre-training procedure. We also demonstrate a regime with a mismatch between the value of the test error and representation quality, and propose an application of our theory to active fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a high-dimensional statistical theory for low-rank adaptation (LoRA) in attention models, emphasizing the dynamics of pre-training and fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: To understand the interaction between pre-training and fine-tuning in attention models and to improve LoRA's effectiveness in low-data scenarios.
AI.method: A solvable framework was developed for a single-head attention layer undergoing pre-training followed by a rank-one LoRA update, analyzed in the high-dimensional limit.
AI.result: The study yields explicit predictions for test errors and representation alignment, revealing an effective noise term that characterizes the influence of pre-training on LoRA.
AI.conclusion: The research outlines optimal pre-training procedures and highlights a scenario where test error and representation quality metrics diverge, paving the way for active fine-tuning applications.

title: NAVIRA: Decoupled Stochastic Remasking for Masked Diffusion Language Models
summary: Masked diffusion language models generate text by iteratively unmasking many tokens in parallel, but this speed comes with a correction problem: tokens generated in the same step are predicted from marginal distributions, and early local dependency errors can later contaminate the context. PRISM addresses this by learning token-level quality scores and remasking unreliable tokens, but its inference rule is coupled: the same forward pass both detects low-quality tokens and computes logits for their replacements, so the erroneous tokens still condition regeneration. We propose NAVIRA, an inference-time decoding policy that separates these two operations and samples remasking positions stochastically. A first forward pass scores tokens; selected tokens are masked; a second forward pass regenerates from the cleaned context. Temperature-controlled remasking reduces repeated correction of the same positions and balances fluency against diversity. In controlled experiments with a 170M masked diffusion language model, decoupling improves fluency, while scheduled stochastic remasking preserves entropy and achieves stronger LLM-judge scores under larger forward-pass budgets. These results show that remasking policy, not only the learned quality signal, is central to reliable masked-diffusion text generation.

AI.tldr: NAVIRA presents an improved remasking policy for masked diffusion language models, enhancing fluency and diversity in text generation by decoupling quality scoring from regeneration processes.
AI.motivation: Masked diffusion language models face a correction problem where early errors in token generation affect context, necessitating a reliable remasking strategy.
AI.method: NAVIRA utilizes a two-step process where tokens are first scored for quality, then low-quality tokens are masked before regenerating from the cleaned context, allowing for temperature-controlled remasking.
AI.result: Decoupling operations in NAVIRA leads to improvements in fluency, while maintaining entropy and achieving higher quality scores compared to previous methods under larger forward-pass budgets.
AI.conclusion: Remasking policies are crucial for enhancing the reliability of text generation in masked diffusion models, beyond merely learning quality signals.

title: ReCache: Learning Budget-Aware Caching Schedules for Diffusion Models via REINFORCE
summary: Modern diffusion models generate high-quality images and videos, but their iterative denoising process makes inference expensive. Feature caching accelerates sampling by reusing or predicting intermediate activations across neighboring denoising steps, exploiting the redundancy of computations along the reverse trajectory. In this work, we focus on the caching schedule: selecting which denoising steps should be fully recomputed. Existing schedules are either fixed (e.g. uniform) or chosen adaptively from per-step error heuristics; in both cases, the actual compute cost is a side-effect of hand-tuned thresholds rather than a quantity the user can specify. We propose ReCache, which inverts this: given a target budget k, it learns the recomputation schedule that maximizes generation quality, turning compute into a directly controllable input. ReCache trains via policy gradients, sidestepping backpropagation through full diffusion inference, and uses no labelled data. Generations from uncached inference serve as matching targets, paired with a reward for generation quality. ReCache is compatible with any caching mechanism, including feature reuse and feature forecasting; for each mechanism, a single trained policy adapts across computational budgets at inference time. ReCache consistently outperforms scheduling baselines: under a $\times5.04$ FLOPs reduction on FLUX, it reduces LPIPS by 31% (from 0.456 to 0.316) compared to DiCache; on Wan 2.1 at a $\sim \times2.6$ speedup, it drops LPIPS by 65% (from 0.480 to 0.169) and boosts the VBench score by 7% (5.6 points, from 70.4 to 76.0) over uniform HiCache. Code is available at https://github.com/thecrazymage/ReCache.

AI.tldr: ReCache is a novel approach to improve the efficiency of diffusion models by learning a caching schedule for recomputation, allowing control over compute costs and enhancing image quality during inference.
AI.motivation: To address the expensive inference process of diffusion models by enabling users to control compute costs while maximizing generation quality.
AI.method: ReCache learns the optimal recomputation schedule using policy gradients, leveraging uncached inference as targets for training without requiring labeled data.
AI.result: ReCache demonstrates significant improvements in generation quality, outperforming existing methods with reductions in LPIPS scores and increases in speed and VBench scores at much lower compute costs.
AI.conclusion: ReCache provides a flexible and efficient mechanism for improving the performance of diffusion models, adapting caching strategies based on user-defined compute budgets.

title: FontFusion: Enhancing Generative Text in Diffusion Models with Typographic Conditioning
summary: Typography generation in diffusion models faces a persistent trade-off: enabling precise font control typically degrades text legibility, while maintaining readability often sacrifices typographic fidelity. We present FontFusion, a plug-and-play conditioning framework for Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architectures that resolves this dilemma through three core innovations: (1) a hierarchical token representation establishing explicit text-font relationships at multiple granularities, (2) position-aware embeddings creating spatial bindings between typography and image content, and (3) a multi-level token dropping strategy improving both computational efficiency and generalization to unseen fonts. Our systematic evaluation of font embedding spaces reveals that a dual encoder combining DeepFont and DINOv2 outperforms any single encoder for typography tasks. FontFusion demonstrates 76% relative improvement on challenging decorative fonts over single-encoder baselines and font consistency gains exceeding approximately 68-76% over unconditioned models, while integrating into existing DiT architectures without retraining.

AI.tldr: FontFusion improves typography generation in diffusion models by balancing font control and text legibility through innovative techniques.
AI.motivation: To address the trade-off in typography generation between font control and text legibility.
AI.method: FontFusion employs a hierarchical token representation, position-aware embeddings, and a multi-level token dropping strategy to enhance typography generation in DiT architectures.
AI.result: FontFusion achieves a 76% relative improvement on decorative fonts and significant font consistency gains over unconditioned models.
AI.conclusion: The framework can be integrated into existing DiT architectures seamlessly, offering enhanced performance without the need for retraining.

title: Addressing Imbalance in Multi-Label Data via Label-Specific Distance-based Oversampling
summary: The complex imbalanced label distribution poses a crucial challenge to multi-label classification, as most classifiers are biased towards the majority class and high-frequent labels. Oversampling is an efficient and flexible solution that augments instances to provide a more balanced training dataset for multi-label classifiers. Most existing oversampling methods create synthetic instances in a heuristic way that essentially relies on neighborhood information retrieved using Euclidean distance within the entire feature space. However, they fail to consider the varying semantic relevance of features to different labels, leading to label inconsistency among proximate neighbors and further introducing label confusion and overfitting to synthetic instances. To overcome the above issue, we propose a novel sampling approach called Label-Specific Distance-based Multi-Label Oversampling (LSDMLO) that creates more useful and well-labeled synthetic instances to address the imbalance in multi-label datasets. LSDMLO derives the label-specific distance to identify label-consistent neighbors based on the weighted pertinent feature space, which facilitates selecting seed instances that express more label correlations in boundary areas and generating synthetic instances aligned with the label distribution of original data. The comprehensive experiments verify that the proposed LSDMLO outperforms the state-of-the-art multi-label sampling approaches under various base classifiers.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces LSDMLO, a novel oversampling method for multi-label classification that addresses imbalanced label distribution by creating label-consistent synthetic instances.
AI.motivation: To tackle bias towards majority classes in multi-label classification caused by imbalanced label distribution and improve synthetic instance quality.
AI.method: The proposed LSDMLO uses label-specific distances in a weighted pertinent feature space to select label-consistent neighbors and generate synthetic instances.
AI.result: LSDMLO outperforms existing state-of-the-art multi-label sampling methods across various base classifiers according to comprehensive experimental results.
AI.conclusion: The novel approach effectively mitigates label confusion and overfitting in synthetic instances, improving the balance in multi-label datasets.

title: VZCrash: A Large-Scale IMU Dataset of Ego-Vehicle Crashes
comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITSC 2026). VZCrash is publicly available at this URL: https://huggingface.co/datasets/vzc-research-chapter/VZCrash
summary: We introduce VZCrash, the largest publicly available dataset of real-world vehicle collision data featuring Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) telemetry. The dataset contains more than 31,000 validated crashes and 158,000 negative samples, including hard cases and distractors. Each sample includes acceleration and angular velocity at 100 Hz, and GPS speed at 1 Hz. Events in VZCrash were captured by devices installed on a fleet of 73,010 commercial vehicles of different sizes driving in the United States over the span of several years. We also present an extensive experimental study enabled by the volume of the dataset. We first benchmark several different approaches, from a simple threshold-based heuristic to state-of-the-art deep learning models. Then, we present an experiment demonstrating the importance of scaling data to train high-quality crash detection models, and we show that scale is especially important when these models need to be deployed into a real-world environment.

AI.tldr: VZCrash is a large dataset of vehicle collision data with IMU telemetry, comprising 31,000 crashes and 158,000 samples; it enables benchmarking models for crash detection.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive dataset for improving crash detection models using real-world data and IMU telemetry.
AI.method: The study benchmarks various crash detection approaches, including heuristic and deep learning models, and emphasizes the significance of data scale in model training.
AI.result: The experimental study demonstrates that scaling the dataset is critical for developing effective crash detection systems, especially for real-world applications.
AI.conclusion: VZCrash offers valuable insights and a robust foundation for advancing vehicle crash detection technologies.

title: English-to-Prakrit Machine Translation via Multilingual Transfer Learning
summary: We study English-to-Prakrit machine translation in a low-resource setting where the target language is unsupported by IndicTrans2. We adapt the multilingual model by mapping Prakrit to the Hindi language tag (hin_Deva) without modifying the tokenizer, vocabulary, or architecture. Using a 1,474-pair Maharashtri Prakrit parallel corpus and evaluation on a 20-sample Ardhamagadhi test set, we report corpus BLEU improvements over an untuned baseline. The results indicate that script-compatible language routing can enable feasible transfer to unsupported classical languages, while highlighting limitations due to data scarcity and dialect mismatch. Our code and trained models are released to the public for further exploration https://github.com/D3v1s0m/indictrans2-prakrit-mt.

AI.tldr: This study explores English-to-Prakrit machine translation in a low-resource context by adapting a multilingual model, achieving improved translation scores despite challenges in data availability.
AI.motivation: To develop machine translation capabilities for Prakrit, a classical language lacking dedicated resources and support from existing translation frameworks like IndicTrans2.
AI.method: Adaptation involved mapping Prakrit to the Hindi language tag in a multilingual model without altering its tokenizer or architecture, utilizing a parallel corpus for training and evaluation.
AI.result: Achieved corpus BLEU score improvements over a baseline model, demonstrating effectiveness despite resource limitations, using a specific parallel corpus and a small evaluation set.
AI.conclusion: Script-compatible routing can facilitate the transfer of machine translation techniques to unsupported languages, though challenges remain due to limited data and dialect issues.

title: Short paper: Models in the dark -- Rectification and erasure under GDPR in ML supply chains
comment: accepted for presentation at Annual Privacy Forum 2026
summary: The rights to rectification and erasure, as established under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), are central to protecting individuals' privacy. However, their effective enforcement in machine learning (ML) systems remains challenging. Existing work has largely addressed these rights from either a legal or a technical perspective in isolation and disregards the fact that models are produced in complex supply chains involving multiple actors across development, distribution, and deployment. This paper presents a holistic survey of challenges in implementing the rights to rectification and erasure in ML models. Drawing on academic literature and guidance from data protection authorities, we find that many GDPR requirements cannot yet be technically met in practice. Our findings further suggest that issues arising in ML supply chains are insufficiently addressed in research. To tackle this gap, we introduce the notion of models in the dark -- derived models created further downstream in an ML chain without sufficient transparency or traceability -- and analyse the urgent challenges posed by this phenomenon. By adopting an interdisciplinary perspective, this work contributes to bridging the gap between legal requirements and the technical implementation of data subject rights in ML, ultimately supporting the development of trustworthy artificial intelligence.

AI.tldr: This paper surveys challenges in implementing GDPR rights of rectification and erasure in machine learning systems, emphasizing the lack of technical compliance and transparency in ML supply chains.
AI.motivation: To address the complex intersection of legal frameworks (GDPR) and technical practices in machine learning, focusing on privacy rights enforcement.
AI.method: Holistic survey of literature and guidance from data protection authorities, highlighting technical challenges and issues in ML supply chains.
AI.result: Identification of gaps where GDPR compliance is not feasible in practice, particularly in the context of ML supply chains and the concept of 'models in the dark.'
AI.conclusion: The study advocates for interdisciplinary approaches to enhance the implementation of data subject rights, promoting more trustworthy AI systems.

title: IA-RAG: Interval-Algebra-Driven Temporal Reasoning for Dynamic Knowledge Retrieval
comment: 22 pages, 10 figures, 13 tables. Code available at https://github.com/xiaoAugenstern/LogicalRAG_TemporalQA
summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has shown strong effectiveness in grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) with external knowledge. However, existing RAG and Graph RAG frameworks largely treat knowledge as static or associate time with coarse-grained timestamps or metadata, failing to capture rich temporal structures such as duration, overlap, and containment. We propose IA-RAG, a hierarchical temporal RAG framework that models knowledge as time intervals and performs retrieval under formal temporal constraints. IA-RAG represents facts as Interval Event Units (IEUs) and organizes them into a hierarchical Thematic Forest, where temporal dependencies are governed by Allen's Interval Algebra. To handle incomplete or uncertain temporal boundaries, IA-RAG further introduces a Sub-graph Time Tightening mechanism that refines fuzzy intervals through logical constraints within connected event subgraphs. In addition, IA-RAG supports implicit temporal semantic retrieval through interval-algebra-guided traversal. Experiments on multiple temporal question answering benchmarks, including TimeQA, TempReason, and ComplexTR, demonstrate that IA-RAG achieves strong temporal retrieval and reasoning performance, particularly on complex compositional temporal reasoning tasks. Our code is released at https://github.com/xiaoAugenstern/LogicalRAG_TemporalQA.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces IA-RAG, a novel framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation that incorporates hierarchical temporal structures to improve temporal knowledge retrieval and reasoning in LLMs.
AI.motivation: Existing RAG frameworks inadequately model the complexity of temporal knowledge, limiting the effectiveness of language models in temporal reasoning tasks.
AI.method: IA-RAG models knowledge as time intervals using Interval Event Units (IEUs) structured in a Thematic Forest, applying Allen's Interval Algebra to govern temporal dependencies. It introduces a Sub-graph Time Tightening mechanism to refine uncertain temporal boundaries and supports implicit retrieval through interval-algebra-guided traversal.
AI.result: IA-RAG demonstrates significant improvements in temporal retrieval and reasoning across various benchmarks, especially excelling in complex compositional temporal reasoning tasks.
AI.conclusion: By effectively modeling temporal aspects of knowledge, IA-RAG enhances the capability of LLMs in addressing temporal queries, showing promising results in the proposed experiments.

title: Knowledge Distillation for Visual Autoregressive Models
summary: Autoregressive (AR) image generation models are highly expressive but computationally intensive, motivating effective model compression. Knowledge distillation (KD) is a natural approach for model compression and has been widely studied in language modeling, yet its behavior in visual AR generation remains underexplored. In this work, we present the first systematic study of distillation strategies for AR image models. Our analysis shows that while standard distillation can yield meaningful gains, recent methods developed for language do not directly transfer to images: long decoding horizons and visual token ambiguity make teacher supervision unreliable especially under student-conditioned contexts. To address this, we propose VarKD, a distillation framework for visual autoregressive models that distills on student samples while selectively applying teacher supervision and reducing token-level ambiguity. Experiments on ImageNet across multiple AR backbones show that VarKD consistently outperforms prior distillation baselines, narrowing the gap to large-scale models.

AI.tldr: This paper presents VarKD, a novel distillation framework for autoregressive image generation models, addressing challenges in transferring knowledge from language models to images, and demonstrating improved performance on ImageNet.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to investigate and improve knowledge distillation methods for autoregressive image generation models, addressing the computational intensity of these models.
AI.method: The authors propose VarKD, a distillation framework tailored for visual autoregressive models. It focuses on distilling knowledge from the teacher model based on student-generated samples and selectively applying teacher supervision to minimize token-level ambiguity.
